factory_decisions.decision: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no framework, no bundler, no transpiler
factory_decisions.context: Infrastructure manifest explicitly specifies framework type 'none'. Vision scope declares 'zero dependencies' as a portfolio signal.
alternatives_considered: Vite + vanilla — rejected: adds build step, node_modules dependency tree, complexity with no user benefit for a <100KB static page
factory_decisions.rationale: The absence of a framework IS the design. Clean source code viewable with View Source. Sub-100KB total weight. No build step required. Vitest used for dev testing only — not shipped.

factory_decisions.decision: Inter from Google Fonts CDN with font-display: swap
factory_decisions.context: Design pass-3 specifies Inter as the single typeface. Infrastructure manifest confirms Google Fonts source.
alternatives_considered: Self-hosted Inter — rejected: adds file management, same result, Google CDN has better cache hit rates
System font stack only — rejected: design spec requires a specific typeface for portfolio-quality typography
factory_decisions.rationale: Inter is free, CDN-cached, excellent legibility, wide weight range. font-display: swap prevents FOIT. Preconnect hints for fast loading.

factory_decisions.decision: CSS custom properties on :root for all design tokens (no preprocessor)
factory_decisions.context: Design pass-3 provides exact color values, typography scale, spacing grid. Need a token system for consistency.
alternatives_considered: CSS preprocessor (Sass/Less) — rejected: adds build step, violates no-framework constraint
Inline values everywhere — rejected: no single source of truth, harder to maintain
factory_decisions.rationale: Native CSS custom properties work in all modern browsers, no build step, tokens are inspectable in DevTools, single source of truth matching the design spec exactly.

factory_decisions.decision: State management via data-state attribute on game container, CSS-driven visibility
factory_decisions.context: Game has 5 states (ready, playing, revealing, game-over, deck-complete). Elements show/hide per state.
alternatives_considered: Class-based toggling per element — rejected: verbose, error-prone, requires JS for every show/hide
JS-driven display toggling — rejected: CSS can handle state-based visibility declaratively
factory_decisions.rationale: Single data-state attribute controls all visibility via CSS selectors [data-state="X"] .element { display: none }. Game logic only needs to call setAttribute once per state change. Clean separation of concerns.

factory_decisions.decision: Card back uses CSS repeating-linear-gradient crosshatch pattern
factory_decisions.context: Design pass-3 specifies 'repeating diagonal lines or crosshatch using repeating-linear-gradient' with base #3D3632 and accent rgba(245, 240, 235, 0.08).
alternatives_considered: SVG pattern — rejected: adds asset, more complex
Solid color — rejected: design spec says 'not a solid color', must register as intentional
factory_decisions.rationale: Pure CSS, zero file weight, matches spec exactly. Two overlapping 45deg/-45deg repeating gradients at 8px spacing with 1px accent lines.

factory_decisions.decision: Vitest + jsdom for testing (dev dependency only, not shipped)
factory_decisions.context: Need test infrastructure for TDD. Product is vanilla JS but tests need DOM environment.
alternatives_considered: No tests — rejected: TDD is required by foundation protocol
Jest — rejected: vitest is faster, native ESM support, lighter config
Playwright/browser tests — rejected: overkill for unit/DOM tests at this stage
factory_decisions.rationale: Vitest gives fast test execution with jsdom environment. Tests read the actual HTML/CSS files and parse them. 42 tests run in <500ms. Not included in production build.

factory_decisions.decision: Card flip uses CSS 3D transform with perspective 1000px, 400ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1.0)
factory_decisions.context: Design pass-3 interaction spec defines exact flip parameters. Foundation scaffolds the CSS; game-logic stories trigger it.
alternatives_considered: JavaScript animation — rejected: CSS transforms are GPU-accelerated, simpler, match the spec
Web Animations API — rejected: CSS is sufficient and more maintainable for a single transform
factory_decisions.rationale: CSS 3D transforms with backface-visibility: hidden on both faces. Flip triggered by adding .flipped class to .card-inner. Easing decelerates like a physical card. Foundation provides the CSS plumbing; feature stories add the trigger logic.

factory_decisions.decision: Test fixtures provide SUITS, VALUES, makeCard(), makeDeck(), and sampleCards for all feature tests
factory_decisions.context: Feature stories need consistent card data for testing. Deck model tests need a full 52-card deck. Comparison tests need specific card pairs.
alternatives_considered: Inline test data per test file — rejected: duplication, inconsistency
JSON fixture files — rejected: less flexible than JS functions that generate test data
factory_decisions.rationale: Exported functions and constants that feature tests import. makeCard(value, suitIndex) produces any card. makeDeck() produces a full 52-card deck. sampleCards provides named realistic examples (Ace of Spades, Seven of Hearts, etc.).

factory_decisions.decision: github-pages-config: static deployment with flat file structure at root
factory_decisions.context: Infrastructure manifest specifies github-pages deployment. No build step, no output directory — files served directly from root.

decided.reason: No framework, no build step. index.html, style.css, game.js served directly from root. .nojekyll file present. GitHub Pages Source = gh-pages branch.

factory_decisions.rationale: Simplest possible deployment. No basePath needed since files are at root. .nojekyll prevents Jekyll processing.

factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for f-scaffold story
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 0 BUILD, 0 EXTEND, 4 REUSE, 0 REFACTOR-THEN-BUILD tasks. All 4 f-scaffold ACs are fully satisfied by existing foundation code. Added 16 targeted tests to verify each AC. No new implementation code needed — foundation phase already built everything.

factory_decisions.decision: f-auth story verified as correctly 'none' — no implementation needed, only verification tests
factory_decisions.context: Infrastructure manifest specifies auth strategy 'none'. Task ledger ACs (registration, login, logout, protected routes, session persistence) are generic foundation ACs that do not apply to this single-player anonymous game.
alternatives_considered: Skip without tests — rejected: TDD protocol requires test evidence even for no-op stories
Implement stub auth — rejected: would add unnecessary code for a game with no users or protected resources
factory_decisions.rationale: Wrote 13 verification tests confirming: no auth forms/buttons, no session tokens, no cookies, no auth providers, no protected routes, no redirect logic. Tests prove the absence is intentional and complete, not accidental. Game is immediately playable without authentication. localStorage used only for best score.

factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for f-ui-shell story (cycle 1, story-building phase)

AC1 (app shell renders): index.html has game container with data-state='ready', all UI regions present — 9 tests in shell.test.js verify. AC5 (loading states): correctly absent per design analysis (no data fetching), divergence documented. No new implementation code or tests needed — foundation phase built everything. 20 existing tests all pass.

factory_decisions.decision: Search Before Building audit for deck-and-card-model story
factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for deck-and-card-model story (cycle 1, game-logic milestone)
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 1 BUILD (deck.js with createDeck, shuffleDeck, drawCard), 0 EXTEND, 1 REFACTOR-THEN-BUILD (fixtures.js duplicated card/deck logic — refactored to import from deck.js). Foundation fixtures already had SUITS, VALUES, makeCard, makeDeck — promoted to production deck.js module and fixtures now re-exports from it. Single source of truth for card model.

factory_decisions.decision: deck.js is an ES module with named exports, consistent with test fixtures pattern
factory_decisions.context: game.js uses IIFE pattern (no modules, runs in browser). deck.js needs to be importable by both tests and game.js.
alternatives_considered: IIFE pattern matching game.js — rejected: tests import deck functions via ESM, IIFE would require global pollution or separate test harness
CommonJS — rejected: vitest uses ESM, project has no bundler to transform CJS
factory_decisions.rationale: deck.js exports via ESM for test imports. When game-state-machine story wires deck into game.js, it will either inline the functions or use a script type=module approach. The deck module is the canonical implementation; game.js will consume it. This keeps tests clean and the implementation reusable.

factory_decisions.decision: Fisher-Yates shuffle returns new array, does not mutate input
factory_decisions.context: Shuffle algorithm choice for AC-FA1-02. Need randomized deck without losing original order.
alternatives_considered: In-place shuffle (mutate) — rejected: callers may want to preserve original deck order for comparison or restart
Sort with random comparator — rejected: not uniform distribution, O(n log n) vs O(n)
factory_decisions.rationale: Fisher-Yates is the standard O(n) uniform shuffle. Returning a new array (slice + swap) prevents accidental mutation bugs in game state management. Test verifies uniformity over 1000 shuffles.

factory_decisions.decision: drawCard returns {card, remainingDeck} — immutable draw pattern
factory_decisions.context: AC-FA1-03 requires draw to deplete deck. Need to decide mutate vs. return-new.
alternatives_considered: Mutate deck array in place (shift/pop) — rejected: mutable state is error-prone for game state management, harder to test
Deck class with internal state — rejected: adds class abstraction where plain functions suffice (McKinley: boring technology)
factory_decisions.rationale: Returning {card, remainingDeck} lets game state management be explicit. Caller replaces their deck reference. Empty deck returns {card: null, remainingDeck: []}. Simple, testable, no hidden state.

factory_decisions.decision: Search Before Building audit for game-state-machine story
factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for game-state-machine story (cycle 1, game-logic milestone)
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 1 BUILD (game-engine.js — pure state machine module), 1 EXTEND (game.js — refactored from IIFE to ES module importing game-engine.js), 0 REUSE, 0 REFACTOR-THEN-BUILD. deck.js already provides createDeck/shuffleDeck/drawCard used by engine. fixtures.js re-exports from deck.js for tests.

factory_decisions.decision: Separate pure game engine (game-engine.js) from DOM wiring (game.js)
factory_decisions.context: State machine logic needs to be testable without DOM. game.js was an IIFE that couldn't be imported by tests.
alternatives_considered: All logic inline in game.js — rejected: untestable without full DOM setup, mixes concerns
Class-based state machine — rejected: plain functions with immutable state are simpler (McKinley: boring technology), and match deck.js pattern
factory_decisions.rationale: game-engine.js exports createGame() returning an immutable state object with transition methods (startGame, guess, resolveWith, restartWith). Each method returns a new state object. compareCards is a pure function. This separation enables 39 unit tests without DOM, plus 24 DOM integration tests. game.js imports the engine and wires DOM events.

factory_decisions.decision: Convert game.js from IIFE to ES module, update script tag to type=module
factory_decisions.context: game-engine.js and deck.js are ES modules. game.js needs to import from them. Prior decision noted this integration point.
alternatives_considered: Inline engine code into game.js IIFE — rejected: violates separation of concerns, code duplication with deck.js
Use a bundler to compile modules to IIFE — rejected: adds build step, violates no-framework constraint
factory_decisions.rationale: ES modules work natively in all modern browsers. type=module on script tag enables import syntax. The module defers automatically (no blocking). Broke auth.test.js which was eval()ing game.js — fixed by removing the eval (auth tests only verify absence of auth patterns in source, don't need script execution).

factory_decisions.decision: Immutable state transitions — every transition returns new state object
factory_decisions.context: Game state machine needs predictable, testable transitions. deck.js already uses immutable pattern (shuffleDeck returns new array, drawCard returns {card, remainingDeck}).
alternatives_considered: Mutable state object — rejected: harder to test, harder to debug, prior factory_decision established immutable pattern with drawCard
factory_decisions.rationale: Each state transition (startGame, guess, resolveWith, restartWith) returns a new state object. The caller replaces their reference. This matches the drawCard immutable pattern and makes every state transition independently testable. 39 unit tests verify all transition paths.

factory_decisions.decision: Search Before Building audit for higher-lower-comparison story
factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for higher-lower-comparison story (cycle 1, game-logic milestone)
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 0 BUILD, 0 EXTEND, 8 REUSE, 0 REFACTOR-THEN-BUILD tasks. All 8 ACs (AC-FA1-13 through AC-FA1-20) are fully satisfied by existing code from the game-state-machine story. compareCards() in game-engine.js:5-11 handles all comparison logic. resolveWith() handles streak increment (correct), streak preservation (wrong/push), and cards-remaining tracking. game.js renderStreak() and renderCardsRemaining() handle DOM updates. Added 30 targeted tests verifying each AC with exact scenarios from the spec.

factory_decisions.decision: resolveWith takes explicit game state parameter rather than using this
factory_decisions.context: Need to resolve reveals after animation delay. Tests need to inject specific card combinations for deterministic testing.
alternatives_considered: resolve() using this — rejected: harder to test with specific card combinations, animation timing couples state to DOM
factory_decisions.rationale: resolveWith(gameState) lets tests inject exact currentCard/nextCard/guessDirection combinations for deterministic testing of correct/wrong/push/deck-complete paths. In production code, game.js calls engine.resolveWith(engine) after animation completes.

factory_decisions.decision: Search Before Building audit for score-persistence story
factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for score-persistence story (cycle 1, game-logic milestone)
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 0 BUILD, 0 EXTEND, 6 REUSE, 0 REFACTOR-THEN-BUILD tasks. All 6 ACs (AC-FA1-21 through AC-FA1-26) are fully satisfied by existing code from the game-state-machine story. game.js:33-48 readBestScore/writeBestScore with try/catch for graceful degradation. game.js:70-76 renderBestScore handles null/isNew display logic. game.js:109-118 game-over render path computes isNew, writes if beaten, displays correct text. Added 33 targeted tests verifying each AC.

factory_decisions.decision: Search Before Building audit for css-card-rendering story
factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for css-card-rendering story (cycle 1, visual-presentation milestone)
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 1 BUILD (card-renderer.js — new module for structured HTML card face rendering with pip layouts, corner labels, face card typography), 1 EXTEND (game.js — replaced inline renderCard with import of renderCardFace from card-renderer.js), 2 REUSE (AC-FA2-04 card back pattern already in style.css, AC-FA2-05 aspect ratio already defined). Also extended style.css with card face CSS (corners, pip grid, value/suit styling, suit color via data-suit-color attribute). Updated game-flow-integration.test.js to include card-renderer functions in JSDOM combined script.

factory_decisions.decision: Separate card-renderer.js module for card face rendering
factory_decisions.context: Card face rendering needs structured HTML (corner labels, pip grids, face card typography) — too complex for inline in game.js, needs to be testable independently.
alternatives_considered: Inline rendering in game.js — rejected: would make game.js too large, mix rendering concerns with game logic, harder to test
Template literals in HTML — rejected: static HTML can't handle dynamic card values and pip counts
factory_decisions.rationale: card-renderer.js exports renderCardFace(el, card) which creates structured DOM: corner labels (top-left, bottom-right), pip grid for number cards (2-10), card-value + card-suit for face cards (J/Q/K/A), large center-suit for Aces. Sets data-suit-color attribute for CSS color targeting. Uses innerHTML='' for cleanup (safe — no user input). Follows same ES module pattern as deck.js and game-engine.js.

factory_decisions.decision: Pip layout uses CSS Grid with predefined position map
factory_decisions.context: Number cards (2-10) need traditional playing card pip arrangements. Pips must be HTML elements positioned to match standard card layouts.
alternatives_considered: Flexbox layout — rejected: traditional pip arrangements (e.g., 7 of hearts with center pip) don't map to linear flex layouts
Absolute positioning — rejected: harder to maintain, doesn't scale with card size
SVG — rejected: spec requires HTML/CSS only, no images
factory_decisions.rationale: PIP_POSITIONS maps card values 2-10 to [col, row] grid positions. CSS Grid (3 columns x 9 rows) handles all layouts. Bottom-half pips get .pip-inverted class for 180deg rotation (traditional card design). Grid scales naturally with card size. Each pip is a <span class='pip'> containing the suit symbol character.

factory_decisions.decision: Suit color driven by data-suit-color attribute on card-front
factory_decisions.context: Card faces need warm red for hearts/diamonds and near-black for clubs/spades. Need a clean way to apply color from JS.
alternatives_considered: Inline style.color only — rejected: works but doesn't allow CSS-based targeting for future enhancements
CSS class toggle — rejected: data attribute is more semantic and matches existing data-state pattern
factory_decisions.rationale: renderCardFace sets data-suit-color='red' or 'dark' on the card-front element. CSS rules .card-front[data-suit-color='red'] { color: var(--color-suit-red) } target suit color via tokens. Also sets inline style.color as a backup. Matches the data-state pattern already used for game state. Tests verify the attribute is set correctly for all four suits.

factory_decisions.decision: Search Before Building audit for game-ui-layout story
factory_decisions.context: Pre-implementation code reuse analysis for game-ui-layout story (visual-presentation milestone)
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 0 BUILD, 0 EXTEND, 5 REUSE, 0 REFACTOR-THEN-BUILD tasks. All 5 ACs (AC-FA2-13 through AC-FA2-17) are fully satisfied by existing foundation CSS. AC-FA2-13 (single-column layout): .game has display:flex, flex-direction:column, align-items:center. AC-FA2-14 (mobile-first 375px): card min-width 140px, btn min-height 48px, card width uses min(200px, 50vw), padding 48px 24px. AC-FA2-15 (desktop max-width): .game has max-width:480px, margin:0 auto. AC-FA2-16 (equal buttons): .btn-higher/.btn-lower use flex:1 in flex container with 16px gap. AC-FA2-17 (no scroll): 100dvh with justify-content:center, compact padding. Added 21 verification tests, all pass immediately.

factory_questions.question: Foundation needs to create GitHub repo and deploy to gh-pages but git push and gh CLI commands are blocked by the session permission system.
suggested_alternatives: Grant git push permissions in this session
Manually push: git push origin main && npx -y gh-pages@6 -d . -b gh-pages --dotfiles
factory_questions.impact: Blocks staging deployment verification. All local foundation work is complete. Feature cycles can proceed once push permissions are available.

factory_questions.question: f-auth acceptance criteria (registration, login, logout, protected routes, session persistence) are generic foundation ACs that don't apply when auth strategy is 'none'. Should these ACs be removed from the task ledger for projects with no auth?
factory_questions.resolved_as: Verified absence with 13 tests. Story passes as 'auth correctly absent' rather than 'auth implemented'. The generic ACs serve as a checklist reminder — for this project, the correct implementation IS no implementation.

divergences.spec_says: f-ui-shell: Navigation includes links for all feature areas
divergences.actually_did: No navigation links. This is a single-page game with one URL and state-based transitions. There are no routes or feature-area pages to link to.
divergences.rationale: The product has zero navigation by design (vision.json scope.out includes 'multi-page routing', design pass-1 confirms 'No navigation. Single page, single URL.'). Navigation links would be scope creep.

divergences.spec_says: f-ui-shell: Error boundaries catch and display errors / Loading states exist for async operations
divergences.actually_did: No error boundaries or loading states implemented. The product has no async operations, no network requests, no data fetching. Page renders instantly from static HTML (<100KB).
divergences.rationale: Design pass-2 five-state analysis confirms: 'No loading state in the traditional sense — entire game is client-side with zero data fetching' and 'No error states exist in this product — no network requests, no API calls.' Error boundaries and loading states are structurally unnecessary.
